lead: Steep slopes, viewpoints and a strong community memory, with views over the whole of Barcelona.
text: It owes its name to the sanctuary of Nuestra Señora del Monte Carmelo, built in 1864 at the foot of the hill, previously known as the Turó d'en Móra. Until the 1920s it was a rural place; after the Civil War it grew with the arrival of people from all over Spain, and the last shacks were not demolished until 1990.

The slope is its most recognisable feature, and its character too: a neighbourhood with a strong association scene, with shops and services, the Parc del Carmel and the Juan Marsé library. It borders the Park Güell, although that belongs to the district of Gràcia. Most of the homes were built between 1960 and 1980, and those of 61 to 90 m² predominate. At 2,858 €/m², its sale price is one of the lowest in the district.
housing: Blocks built between 1960 and 1980, mostly of 61 to 90 m², and low-rise houses with gardens in the older areas.
